states: Private dev stack at 127.0.0.1 (PR 2741's server on main plus a loopback fake Proxmox API and a test host agent for the same machine): headless Chromium (Playwright on pulse-dev) at 1280x800 and 390x844, plus the built-in browser pane on 2026-10-08 on earlier code. Joined node+agent = one Proxmox node row and no Machines row.

Operator split (POST /api/resources/{id}/report-merge, the drawer's Split merged resource) delivered live by websocket delta with no reload: the Proxmox page keeps one node row (node uptime) and the Machines page lists the agent as its own row; its drawer reads Agent, Debian 12, own primary and machine ID, no node alias or Proxmox context. The last browser pass (2 of 2 completed transitions at 390 and 2 of 2 at 1280; two more runs died at the login field while Vite cold-compiled, before any split) ran on the revision before this commit's final edits to which REST-only fields a rebuilt row keeps (scope evidence for non-host facets, discovery readiness matching); the browser pass does not observe those fields and unit tests with negative controls cover them. Earlier revisions: 2 of 2 at 390 and 3 of 3 at 1280, and 3 of 3 and 3 of 3 before that. Before the fixes in this change the same transition left the agent missing from Machines in 4 of 4 and then 2 of 4 phone-width runs. On main's frontend the split agent was drawn as a second Proxmox node and Machines showed 'No Pulse Agent machines'.

Relink (POST /api/resources/{id}/link) returns the pair to one joined row before every run. Screenshots of the joined, split Proxmox and split Machines states inspected at both widths (earlier code; later runs were checked by row text).
Not covered: a physical phone, other platforms' host rows (Docker, Kubernetes, vSphere, TrueNAS pairs) and an operator unlink through the drawer on the final code.
interactions: Split merged resource dialog opened and confirmed in the built-in browser pane (2026-10-08, earlier code); report-merge and link requests posted for the repeated runs. Proxmox page to Machines page by in-app navigation (no reload) after the split; Machines row expanded to its drawer.
Websocket updates arrive while the page is open; no uncaught page error in the final-code runs (console output was not otherwise captured). All traffic is local to the private stack.
